summary.headline: Xelpmoc Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR10.8 million, up from INR7.1 million a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA still negative at INR15.6 million.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose year on year to INR10.8 million from INR7.1 million but edged down from INR11.2 million in Q3 FY26. Adjusted operating EBITDA was negative INR15.6 million, versus negative INR15.3 million a year ago and negative INR14.9 million in Q3, and net loss narrowed to INR17.8 million including INR2.4 million of ESOP cost. Management says 100% of revenue now comes from corporate clients, with focus on in-house products (DocuXray, RELY) and data science/AI, and it is not onboarding new startups absent exceptional opportunities. Portfolio fair value rose to INR726.8 million at March 31, 2026 from INR631.8 million a year earlier, and management guided that revenue traction should come over the next few quarters without giving numeric targets.

segments.name: Corporate (data science / AI products and services)
segments.commentary: Management stated 100% of revenue is from corporate clients; DocuXray (new avatar of Xtract, generative AI document processing) and RELY (agetech platform) are the focus products. Revenue from RELY is expected to be recognised from the next quarter.

segments.name: Portfolio: Mihup
segments.commentary: Conversation AI platform with contracted ARR of INR1 billion; clients include Tata Motors, Canara HSBC, Angel Broking, Pine Labs; onboarded HDFC in the quarter. Company has taken a partial exit in Mihup.

segments.name: Portfolio: Woovly (Live2.ai)
segments.commentary: Live2.ai SaaS at USD4.1 million ARR with 245 brands, reported as EBITDA positive; enterprise clients include Henkel, L'Oreal, Samsonite, Titan, Decathlon, Unilever.

segments.name: Portfolio: Pencil
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR320 lakhs for January to March 2026; signed a USD950,000 service deal over 36 months.

segments.name: Portfolio: The Star In Me (TSIM)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR3.4 crores in FY26; new clients include 7-Eleven, Cognizant, Hexaware, Salesforce.

segments.name: Portfolio: Kids Stop Press (KSP)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR201 lakhs in FY26; primary audience first-time parents aged 25 to 34 making up 75% of traffic.

segments.name: Portfolio: Biome / Zoop.Money / OsteoForge
segments.commentary: Zoop.Money has over INR300 crores inventory value across 70-plus projects. Biome raised its OsteoForge commitment to INR4 crores from INR2 crores for a 10% combined stake; valuation up 2.5x to INR100 crores in 5 months.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 targets for DocuXray or RELY customers, and no consolidated EBITDA breakeven timeline; management said it cannot disclose future numbers.
Management expects revenue to gradually gain traction over the next few quarters as corporate conversations take time.
Committed to reaching EBITDA profitability as soon as possible; new products are expected to help get there.
RELY numbers expected to be recognised in financials in the next quarter, per Jaison Jose.
Company expects to keep investing in product over the next 2 to 3 years.
capex_capacity: RELY is operating with a couple of hundred residents under management across 6 assisted living centres in western India; pipeline said to be a few times that size for the coming quarter.
Senior living deployments reported at late-stage negotiation, expected to convert within weeks.
Some sitting inventory products in Signal Analytics may be redeployed alongside DocuXray.
Company is not hiring a direct sales team; it works with a couple of GTM partners on revenue share.
demand_pricing: Startup funding remains volatile, slowing new startup revenue; management is concentrating on corporate clients and not onboarding new startups absent exceptional opportunities.
DocuXray: 2 to 3 POCs completed and 2 to 3 ongoing; some small POCs converted to paid monetisation, but POC-to-order conversion is taking longer, especially with larger organisations.
RELY pricing model: per-bed or per-apartment per-month SaaS subscription, typically annual or minimum 2-year contracts.
Signal Analytics is hard to sell given wariness toward EdTech and automated processes; company is exploring corporate training and skill development adjacencies.
Target segments for data science/AI: BFI, real estate and compliance, although product is sector agnostic.

qa_highlights.question: Can management provide FY27 targets for DocuXray and RELY customers and a timeline to consolidated EBITDA breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose future numbers. It described DocuXray as at product-market fit with long sales cycles, and RELY as having onboarded operators, with senior living deployments close to conversion.

qa_highlights.question: What were the outcomes of the data science and AI POCs, and how many converted to orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 2 to 3 POCs were completed and 2 to 3 more were ongoing; 1 or 2 small POCs converted to monetisation, and POC-to-order takes additional time.

qa_highlights.question: Which 3 milestones could close the gap between market valuation and underlying portfolio value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited portfolio value growth, with expectations of 3 to 4 big successes from the portfolio, and a shift to privacy-focused, localised AI products; no timeline was committed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need to hire 100-plus people to reach INR14 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said headcount cannot be directly correlated with revenue because many staff are building products whose revenues have not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash runway?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said runway is about 10 to 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current status of Signal Analytics?
qa_highlights.answer: It is operational but hard to sell; management is pursuing adjacent corporate training and skill development products and redeploying inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current valuation of the startup portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the total value is about INR72.67 crores against about INR792 lakhs invested; he corrected an earlier figure during the call.

risks_watch: Cash runway of about 10 to 12 months implies a likely need for fresh funding or cost action.
Adjusted EBITDA loss remains around INR15 million a quarter with revenue of about INR11 million.
Startup funding volatility could delay portfolio monetisation and new startup revenue.
DocuXray and RELY revenue not yet material; POC-to-order conversion is slow.
Signal Analytics demand weak in EdTech.
Transcript corrections were made during the call: Pencil/TSIM/KSP figures were restated and portfolio value was corrected to INR72.67 crore; watch for consistency in future disclosures.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on near-term revenue, which management says will take quarters, while confident about product traction and the portfolio thesis. Management declined to give forward numbers and deflected several questions on timelines.
